source.original_text: Attributed expanded proof component, not the full Lemma D.4: for an actual Algorithm D.2 proximal query at random center Y, Lemma D.3 bounds the number N_prox(Y) of gradient evaluations by C_c[1+log(1+norm(gradient V(Y))/eps)]. If Y has a probability law and E norm(gradient V(Y))^2 is finite, then the actual count is integrable and Jensen together with the probability-space L2-to-L1 inequality gives E N_prox(Y) <= C_c[1+log(1+sqrt(E norm(gradient V(Y))^2)/eps)]. Samplinglib constructs measurable p and first-stop N from the actual exact-real finite-fuel interpreter, retains its proximal equation, eps-accuracy and successful return with count N+1, and uses the explicit admissible C_c=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c) already derived for D.3. Assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space, V is C2, kappa>=1, kappa^(-1) norm(v)^2 <= D2 V(x)[v,v] <= norm(v)^2, 0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, nu is a probability measure, and y maps to norm(gradient V(y))^2 integrably. The actual Picard center law and numerical D.7 bound, phase counting, D.8, approximate-kernel stability, sampling accuracy and full-paper theorem remain separate. Total variation is not used to transfer unbounded cost.

lean.statement: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}, 1 ≤ κ → ContDiff ℝ 2 V → (∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖^2) → ∀ {eta c eps : ℝ}, 0 < eta → eta ≤ c → c < 1 → 0 < eps → ∀ (ν : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν], Integrable (fun y => ‖gradient V y‖^2) ν → let T := fun y x : E => y - eta • gradient V x; let C := 2 + (1 + Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹)) / (-Real.log c); ∃ p : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ, Measurable p ∧ Measurable N ∧ Measurable (fun y => (T y)^[N y] y) ∧ (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧ ‖(T y)^[N y] y - p y‖ ≤ eps ∧ Q (gradient V) eta eps y (N y+1) y = some ((T y)^[N y] y, N y+1)) ∧ Integrable (fun y => (N y : ℝ)+1) ν ∧ (∫ y, (N y : ℝ)+1 ∂ν) ≤ C * (1 + Real.log (1 + Real.sqrt (∫ y, ‖gradient V y‖^2 ∂ν) / eps))

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space, equipped with a measurable structure whose measurable sets are the Borel sets. Let V:E->R and let kappa be a nonnegative real number. Assume kappa>=1, V is twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and, for every x,v in E, (1/kappa)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2. Let eta,c,eps be real numbers satisfying 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E such that y |-> ||grad V(y)||^2 is integrable. For y in E define T_y:E->E by T_y(x)=y-eta grad V(x), and define C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c). Then there exist measurable functions p:E->E and N:E->N such that y |-> T_y^[N(y)](y) is measurable and, for every y in E, p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y, ||T_y^[N(y)](y)-p(y)||<=eps, and Q(grad V,eta,eps,y,N(y)+1,y)=some((T_y^[N(y)](y),N(y)+1)). Moreover, y |-> N(y)+1 is integrable with respect to nu and integral (N(y)+1) dnu(y) <= C(1+log(1+sqrt(integral ||grad V(y)||^2 dnu(y))/eps)). Here T_y^[n] denotes n-fold iteration (with the zeroth iterate equal to the identity), and Q is the stated exact-real recursive interpreter, so N(y)+1 is the number of gradient-oracle evaluations, including the successful test.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ApproximateProximalExecution
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Integral
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Basic
import Mathlib.Probability.Moments.Variance
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Basic

/-!
# Expected work of actual stopped proximal execution

Chen--Chewi--Lu--Zhang, arXiv:2609.06906v1, Appendix D.2, Lemma D.4:
the Jensen step after (D.7), not the Picard input-moment estimate or total
run cost (D.8). The input law's second moment remains an explicit dependency.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Filter InnerProductSpace
open scoped Topology NNReal

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ProximalExpectedWork

private theorem log_work_integral {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    {μ : Measure α} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {g : α → ℝ}
    (hg : Measurable g) (hgn : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x)
    (hgs : Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2) μ) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    Integrable (fun x => Real.log (1 + g x / eps)) μ ∧
    (∫ x, Real.log (1 + g x / eps) ∂μ) ≤
      Real.log (1 + Real.sqrt (∫ x, g x ^ 2 ∂μ) / eps) := by
  have hLp : MemLp g 2 μ := (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hg.aestronglyMeasurable).mpr hgs
  have hgi : Integrable g μ := hLp.integrable (by norm_num)
  have hpos (x) : 0 < 1 + g x / eps := by have := hgn x; positivity
  have hlog : Integrable (fun x => Real.log (1 + g x / eps)) μ := by
    apply (hgi.div_const eps).mono'
      ((measurable_const.add (hg.div_const eps)).log.aestronglyMeasurable)
    filter_upwards [] with x
    change ‖Real.log (1 + g x / eps)‖ ≤ g x / eps
    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.log_nonneg (le_add_of_nonneg_right
      (div_nonneg (hgn x) heps.le)))]
    have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (hpos x)
    linarith
  refine ⟨hlog, ?_⟩
  have hconc : ConcaveOn ℝ (Set.Ici (1 : ℝ)) Real.log :=
    strictConcaveOn_log_Ioi.concaveOn.subset
      (by intro x hx; exact lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1) hx)
      (convex_Ici 1)
  have hj := hconc.le_map_integral
    (Real.continuousOn_log.mono (fun x hx => ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hx)))
    isClosed_Ici (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => by
      change 1 ≤ 1 + g x / eps
      exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (div_nonneg (hgn x) heps.le)))
      ((integrable_const 1).add (hgi.div_const eps)) hlog
  have hmean : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) ≤ Real.sqrt (∫ x, g x ^ 2 ∂μ) := by
    have hv := ProbabilityTheory.variance_nonneg g μ
    rw [ProbabilityTheory.variance_eq_sub hLp] at hv
    have hs := Real.sq_sqrt (integral_nonneg (μ := μ) (fun x => sq_nonneg (g x)))
    have hn := Real.sqrt_nonneg (∫ x, g x ^ 2 ∂μ)
    change 0 ≤ (∫ x, g x ^ 2 ∂μ) - (∫ x, g x ∂μ)^2 at hv
    nlinarith
  change (∫ x, Real.log (1 + g x / eps) ∂μ) ≤ Real.log (∫ x, 1 + g x / eps ∂μ) at hj
  simp only [integral_add (integrable_const 1) (hgi.div_const eps),
    integral_const, probReal_univ, smul_eq_mul, one_mul, integral_div] at hj
  exact hj.trans (Real.log_le_log (by
    have hn : 0 ≤ ∫ x, g x ∂μ := integral_nonneg hgn
    positivity) (by gcongr))

section
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

/-- The actual stopped gradient program has integrable query count under an
input law with square-integrable gradient, with the D.4 Jensen work bound.
This does not identify that law with the realized Picard centers or prove D.7. -/
theorem approximate_proximal_expected_work {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖^2)
    {eta c eps : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (hec : eta ≤ c) (hc : c < 1) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (ν : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (hmoment : Integrable (fun y => ‖gradient V y‖^2) ν) :
    let T := fun y x : E => y - eta • gradient V x
    let C := 2 + (1 + Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹)) / (-Real.log c)
    ∃ p : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ,
      Measurable p ∧ Measurable N ∧ Measurable (fun y => (T y)^[N y] y) ∧
      (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧
        ‖(T y)^[N y] y - p y‖ ≤ eps ∧
        ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery (gradient V) eta eps y (N y+1) y =
          some ((T y)^[N y] y, N y+1)) ∧
      Integrable (fun y => (N y : ℝ) + 1) ν ∧
      (∫ y, (N y : ℝ) + 1 ∂ν) ≤
        C * (1 + Real.log (1 + Real.sqrt (∫ y, ‖gradient V y‖^2 ∂ν) / eps)) := by
  dsimp only
  obtain ⟨p, N, hp, hN, hout, hall⟩ :=
    ApproximateProximalExecution.approximate_proximal_execution hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps
  have hgcont : Continuous (gradient V) := by
    unfold gradient
    exact (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm.continuous.comp
      (hV.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num))
  have hg : Measurable (fun y => ‖gradient V y‖) := hgcont.norm.measurable
  obtain ⟨hlog, hj⟩ := log_work_integral hg (fun y => norm_nonneg _) hmoment heps
  let C := 2 + (1 + Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹)) / (-Real.log c)
  have hC : 0 ≤ C := by
    have hcp : 0 < c := heta.trans_le hec
    have hd : 0 < 1-c := sub_pos.mpr hc
    have ha : 0 < -Real.log c := neg_pos.mpr (Real.log_neg hcp hc)
    have hb : 0 ≤ Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹) := Real.log_nonneg (by
      have hm := mul_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr hd.le) hcp.le
      have hi := inv_mul_cancel₀ hd.ne'
      nlinarith)
    dsimp [C]
    positivity
  have hbound (y) : (N y : ℝ)+1 ≤ C*(1+Real.log (1+‖gradient V y‖/eps)) :=
    (hall y).2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hdom : Integrable (fun y => C*(1+Real.log (1+‖gradient V y‖/eps))) ν :=
    ((integrable_const 1).add hlog).const_mul C
  have hcount : Integrable (fun y => (N y : ℝ)+1) ν := by
    apply hdom.mono' (by fun_prop)
    filter_upwards [] with y
    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity)]
    exact hbound y
  refine ⟨p, N, hp, hN, hout, fun y => ⟨(hall y).1, (hall y).2.2.2.2.1,
    (hall y).2.2.2.2.2.2⟩, hcount, ?_⟩
  calc
    (∫ y, (N y : ℝ)+1 ∂ν) ≤ ∫ y, C*(1+Real.log (1+‖gradient V y‖/eps)) ∂ν :=
      integral_mono hcount hdom hbound
    _ = C*(1+∫ y, Real.log (1+‖gradient V y‖/eps) ∂ν) := by
      rw [integral_const_mul, integral_add (integrable_const 1) hlog]
      simp
    _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (add_le_add_right hj 1) hC

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ProximalExpectedWork

source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib isolates and expands the expectation/Jensen step; this is not the full Lemma D.4, equation D.7 or equation D.8, and is not the authors' original wording or an endorsement.

candidate_publication_context.statement: Let an actual Algorithm D.2 query at a random center Y have pointwise count N_prox(Y) bounded by C_c[1+log(1+‖∇V(Y)‖/eps)]. If the center law is a probability measure and E‖∇V(Y)‖² is finite, then the actual count is integrable and E[N_prox(Y)]≤C_c[1+log(1+sqrt(E‖∇V(Y)‖²)/eps)]. Samplinglib constructs the measurable first-stopped execution and its count rather than assuming an accurate oracle or a cost random variable. The explicit C_c is the admissible constant already derived for D.3.

sources.scope: Attributed expansion of the expectation/Jensen step, not the full lemma.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra. V:E→R is C², kappa≥1, and kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖² for every x,v. The ContDiff assumption makes fderiv a genuine derivative.
Fix 0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0. No eta≤1/2 restriction is introduced. The explicit constant depends only on c.

nu is a probability measure on E and y↦‖gradient V y‖² is integrable. This moment hypothesis must later be established for the actual Picard center law; it is not silently assumed to follow from proximity in total variation.
lesson.statement: There exist measurable proximal points p and stopping indices N with measurable returned iterate x_N(y), where x_0(y)=y and x_(n+1)(y)=y−eta∇V(x_n(y)). They satisfy p(y)+eta∇V(p(y))=y and ‖x_N(y)−p(y)‖≤eps. The actual finite-fuel interpreter with N(y)+1 fuel returns (x_N(y),N(y)+1). Its real-valued query count is integrable under nu and has the following expectation bound.

steps.title: Use the real stopped program, not an assumed cost certificate
steps.text: The existing execution theorem constructs p and N by contraction and the first successful residual test. Reuse these same witnesses, together with their measurable output, accuracy, and exact interpreter equation. In particular N+1 includes the final successful gradient evaluation.
steps.lean: approximate_proximal_execution supplies hall. Its pointwise work conjunct becomes hbound; its actual execution conjunct is retained in the public conclusion.

steps.title: Establish integrability before taking expectations
steps.text: C² regularity makes the gradient continuous and hence g measurable. The assumed integrable square gives g in L²; on a probability space this implies L¹. The nonnegative logarithm is bounded by g/eps, so it is integrable. The count is measurable, nonnegative, and dominated by an integrable multiple of one plus that logarithm.
steps.lean: memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq and MemLp.integrable supply L¹. Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos and Integrable.mono' prove log integrability; a second domination proves hcount.

steps.title: Apply Jensen on a closed positive domain
steps.text: The variable 1+g/eps lies in [1,infinity). Restrict concavity and continuity of log to this closed convex half-line. Both the variable and its logarithm are integrable, so Mathlib's integral Jensen theorem applies without any improper-log convention.
steps.lean: strictConcaveOn_log_Ioi is restricted to Set.Ici 1; ConcaveOn.le_map_integral checks the domain, closedness and both integrability obligations.

steps.title: Compare the first and second moments
steps.text: Nonnegative variance yields (E g)²≤E(g²). Since g and the square root are nonnegative, E g≤sqrt(E(g²)). This is the Cauchy–Schwarz step on a probability space, using Mathlib's variance identity rather than reproving a generic inequality.

steps.title: Integrate the pointwise work estimate
steps.text: For 0<c<1, both −log c and 1−c are positive, and log((1−c)⁻¹) is nonnegative, so C_c≥0. Integrate the actual count bound, use linearity for the integrable terms, then combine Jensen and log monotonicity. No distributional identification or exchange of limiting integrals is needed.

lesson.lean_statement: The exact adjacent declaration quantifies the input probability measure, genuine curvature bounds, moment hypothesis, constructed interpreter witnesses and integrable expected cost.
lesson.lean_proof: The public proof applies the existing actual-execution theorem. A private helper packages Mathlib Jensen, L²-to-L¹ and variance arguments; it has no separate leaf credit. No assumed accuracy or expected-cost oracle replaces the real program.
